prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1229; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling eastbound and attempting a left turn at an intersection in Sugar Land, Texas, when the front of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, whose vehicle had been proceeding straight through the intersection. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy under which this vehicle is insured, and that status was confirmed at the scene. The Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat and was present in the vehicle at the time of impact, a fact confirmed by both drivers and by responding officers. Driver 1 reported neck strain and stated that the pain began shortly after the collision. Damage to the front bumper, hood, and driver-side headlamp assembly is consistent with the impact described by both parties. Photographs taken at the scene verify several of these details. No independent witnesses were located, and no prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to either driver or observed by responding officers. At this time it is not yet clear whether the reported neck injury resulted from this collision, and no medical evaluation has been completed. Follow-up is recommended.
